gaps.gap: WRITER gap: the block wiring rebuilds each record and re-homes its members, but every member entity remains (also) reachable from the MODEL-SPACE block-table chain in the built file. Codec-side verification cannot see it (the codec's built-file census walks the record chain and reports no model-space members — block_record BIT-EXACT), while Civil 3D's model-space enumeration walks the BTR chain and sees the full member population as loose model-space entities: +343 (Parcel-1A), +371 (Align-6C), +371 (Points-3) native entities per built file, matching the member population EXACTLY per type (Line/Circle/LwPolyline/Text/Insert/Arc/Wipeout/Hatch/Leader/Solid). Member INSERTS additionally appear as 2 extra model-space AcDbBlockReference per file. The wiring round's probe files could not catch this: Labels-1a/2a's members are annotation-light and their 1-3 inserts were LEGITIMATE model-space inserts, so the L2/L3 legs of the wiring probes (if any) had no contrast. First exposed by packet C's L3 equality gate.
gaps.class: WRITER (ownership: the writer must link members ONLY under the rebuilt record's entity chain — either it creates them in model space first and never unlinks, or it writes the owner field and the BTR chain inconsistently)
gaps.implementability: implementable — one ownership fix in the #703 wiring path (the member entities' home BTR must be the rebuilt record, not model space); a regression test should assert the app-visible model-space count (codec census is structurally blind to this class of bug, compare_verify cannot catch it)
gaps.evidence: /tmp/opencode/ct/cap.pktC.p1b.built.census.txt vs p1b.Parcel-1A.dwg.census.txt (+343 == members exactly per type); cap.pktC.p6c.{Align-6C.dwg,built}.census.txt and cap.pktC.p3.{Points-3.dwg,built}.census.txt (+371 each, identical member sets); codec census of the built files (packetC/packetC/*.built.json codec_census) shows NO model-space members — the two walks disagree, which is the bug's signature

gaps.gap: FIXED (packetC-fix2): the built file carried no stale object and the correct 2 station groups — the app-side dead object (id=451 class=AcRxObject ePermanentlyErased, audit null=1) and the census loss (AeccDbAlignmentStationLabeling 2->1) were a REFERENCE-LAYOUT defect: the oracle stores a soft-0/hard-0 reference pair after the alignment hard pointer of every label that carries overrides (Parcel-1A ALG0: one pair; ALG1 'Second Street': two — its begin-mark label and a flipped interior station), and the #688 writer emitted one alignment pointer per label with no pairs. The application walks the reference list per label; on the desync it erases the record. Typed-field compare is structurally blind to it (the class streams of the oracle and the rebuilt record are bit-identical; only the handle/reference section differed). Fix: add_alignment_label_group writes the pair per overridden label. Verified: rebuilt Parcel-1A audit 330/0/0 (was 330/1/0), app census AeccDbAlignmentStationLabeling 2==2 (was 2->1); the minimal 2-alignment+4-group repro (which reproduced the dead object at every file shape and handle assignment) is clean 6/0/0 with Station 2==2. Isolation evidence chain: the dead object followed ALG1's RECORD through build-order reversal and file-shape changes; label-content ablations (removing the negative-station labels, the 0.0-station label, its override) did NOT clear it; the ref-pair fix did.
